To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fluorine substitution on the bisphenol A backbone increases the thermal stability of the final prepolymer.

the fluorinated propargyl ether of 2,2-bis (4-hydroxyphenyl) hexafluoro propane has better thermal properties than the propargyl ether analogue of bisphenol-A and that the degradation of the fluorinated proparylgyl ether occurs in two steps, the first one being related to the degradation of the ether bridge.

the fluorine pivot of the crosslinked compound confers the best heat properties to the crosslinked material, and that the degradation of the compounds occurred as a double step for the diproprargyl ether of dipropargyl bisphenol A, but as a single step in the case of the dipropargylic ether of hexaflourobisphenol-A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the thermal properties of crosslinked compounds based on dipropargyl ethers of bisphenols.

the synthesis of fluorinated prepolymers based on dipropargyl ethers of fluorinated and non-fluorinated bisphenols, with their crosslinking by a Diels-Alder reaction and with the heat stability and degradation of the cross-linked compounds.
the study of new monomers for the synthesis of new crosslinked polymers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fluorine atoms confer better thermal stability to the crosslinked material.
fluorinated compounds have better thermal properties than their non-fluorinated equivalents.
the fluorine atom in hexafluorodipropargyl ether bisphenol A is a very good pivot for crosslinked materials, but that the reactivity of the monomer is lower than that of the non-fluorinated monomer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fluorine atom is a good substituent for the central pivot of a propargyl skeleton, but the presence of a phenolic group in this skeleton leads to the formation of weak links in the crosslinked polymer, especially when the heat treatment is not controlled.
the thermal properties of fluorinated compounds are better than those of non-fluorinated compounds and that these properties are also dependent on the central pivot of their skeleton.
the fluorinated compound is more stable than the non-fluorinated one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fluorination of a phenolic compound has a positive impact on the thermal stability of its propargylic derivative.
the use of a fluorine pivot in the skeleton of the monomers is a good solution for improving the thermal properties of crosslinked materials.
the presence of the fluorine atoms in the molecule increases the stability of the polymer, which can be explained by the higher stability of the C-F bond compared to the C-H bond.
